clues: This town is in the north of Lebanon, in a high hill land. It sits at the head of the Holy Kadisha Valley.
This high hill town has winters that freeze hard each year. That cold helps it keep the country's oldest ski resort and its first ski lift.
Some of the first monks in the East made their homes in its valley long ago. Their faith still fills the town with close to forty churches.
Poet and painter Khalil Gibran was born in this town long ago. A museum here now honors his life and his art.
Its old cedar woods are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. They are the last place the famed cedar of Lebanon grows on its own.
